description: The scope rejections are COMPILE-time in every clause, measured cell by cell on a real account. Two of them: a qualifier naming no FROM-clause key ("invalid identifier 'R.V'") and a bare name carried by BOTH sides of an ON join ("ambiguous column name 'D'"). WHERE, GROUP BY keys, HAVING - inside aggregate ARGUMENTS too - and ORDER BY all reject over EMPTY inputs, and ORDER BY rejects regardless of row count, so a single surviving row must not short-circuit the check away. The countervailing rules are measured too: SELECT aliases are legal names in every one of these clauses, WHERE included, so an alias key never trips the rejection even when the join carries same-named duplicates elsewhere; a USING join's left-preference resolution compiles quietly; and ORDER BY resolves against the SELECT OUTPUT first, so only a key matching no output column falls through to the FROM-scope rules - where a bare ON-join duplicate is then ambiguous even though the output-first rule would have saved the same spelling had the column been selected. Three more shapes ride along: a bare name known nowhere is 'invalid identifier' in every clause; exactly the ANSI set of context functions works WITHOUT parentheses while any other bare function name and CONNECT BY's LEVEL outside a hierarchical query do not; a date/time-unit bareword is legal only in ARGUMENT position; and the output-name visibility rules - a star RENAME target is filterable in WHERE, a lateral column alias is visible only to LATER items so a forward reference is invalid, and a window function's arguments may reference an earlier alias. Converted 1:1 from query/PlanTimeClauseScopeTest (now retired).
